newsitem.title: UK: WEEK AHEAD - Focus on German M3, US note auction.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - Focus on German M3, US note auction.

text.p: Financial markets will focus their attention on key data from Germany and U.S. Treasuries supply next week, analysts said on Friday.
Business sentiment will also keep markets on their toes, with the U.S. Philadelphia Fed Index on Thursday, Britain's CBI survey of monthly trends and Germany's Ifo report also due.

"The German market traded optimistically this week following the weak September output and orders figures but the data coming up have the ability to upset the bullish trend" said Keith Edmonds, chief analyst at IBJ International in London.
German numbers include October M3 and October import and export prices.
IBJ is forecasting increased business confidence, a slight rise in inflation and a modest decline in monetary growth.
Analysts said they would be watching the Philadelphia Fed for any indication that the U.S. economy is less buoyant than in the second quarter.

"For the U.S. market to rally further from here we need to see further evidence of a slowdown. If we don't get any slowdown, it's unlikely we can maintain this bullish market," said Kirit Shah, international economist at First Chicago in London.
Treasuries must also absorb an injection of supply, with two-year notes up for auction on Tuesday and five-year notes on Wednesday."There might be some indigestion there," said Edmonds.
Analysts said they expected U.S. September international trade data on Wednesday to show a smaller deficit than in August, though they did not see the dollar moving higher.
U.S. housing starts for October are out on Tuesday and expected to show a rebound after coming in at only 1.43 million in September, analysts said.
In Britain attention will be on the November CBI survey.
"People will be looking to see if there is any impact from sterling's appreciation on export expectations," said Edmonds.
UK M4 provisional figures for November and October's retail sales will be of interest after last week's unsettling rise in underlying inflation to 3.3 percent.
"The CBI survey and the M4 figures are both likely to show strong money growth and flat to stable production," said Teis Knuthsen, international economist at First Chicago in London.
Analysts said they would be watching the UK October PSBR figures, due on Monday, in the run up to the budget on November 26.
They expected a public sector debt repayment for October but said this was because of cyclical revenue trends rather than an underlying fall in borrowing.
"We have an increasing budget deficit that is not sustainable," said Knuthsen. "We need to see a tightening of fiscal policy in the UK to become bullish on gilts from here."
Italian inflation will be another focus. Analysts said the BTP market would be bullish if consumer price inflation fell below 3.0 percent.
"If we get an indication that CPI is moving below 3.0 percent, the bond market will be gearing up for a rate cut," said Knuthsen.
"It will collide with the fact that the budget is likely to be passed in the lower house and that would mean the final obstacle for Italian re-entry into the ERM is gone," he said.
